title: A genuine JSON-text string at maxDepth is byte-identical to a truncated subtree past maxDepth
rationale: This turns the previous fixture ACCEPTED verdict into a measurable defect. Two structurally different documents produce the SAME flattened map, so the flattened form is non-injective at the depth cliff. Bounding depth is defensible; making the bound output collide with legitimate user data is not.
catchesBugClass: Non-injectivity introduced by a resource bound: the class of bug where a limit output is indistinguishable from ordinary data. Also guards the fix - the moment a truncation marker is added, the collision assertion flips.
cannotCatch: Only detectable as a PAIR. A per-fixture round-trip assertion passes here, so a harness that checks fixtures in isolation reports nothing wrong. It also cannot catch the symmetric collision for arrays.

predicted.detail: This document alone round-trips exactly. The defect is that its flattened form is byte-identical to depth-one-over-max, and the paired assertion is what records it.

configDescription: MapFlattener.builder().maxDepth(3); flat map must equal depth-one-over-max
